capabilities.name: Multi-node routing and port transfer
capabilities.note: Phase 5 seal: the native routing acceptor implements the non-broker ipcz Router state machine (terminal/proxy routers, decaying links, sequenced parcel queues, closure propagation, WithLocalPeer deserialization, SerializeNewRouterAndConfigureProxy + BeginProxyingToNewRouter, AcceptBypassLink, StopProxying teardown, RouterLinkState TryLock/SetSideStable, and the full bridge chain: MergeRoute-equivalent setup, bridge-aware Flush/StopProxyingToLocalPeer/AcceptRouteClosureFrom, and MaybeStartBridgeBypass/StartBridgeBypassFromLocalPeer for all three cases). The acceptor-initiated bridge bypass is reproduced message-for-message (BypassPeerWithLink(1->14), FlushRouter(14), StopProxyingToLocalPeer(14, 0); transfer-back on sublink 15, descriptor new=16) and the official broker's event stream is byte-identical to the oracle-acceptor baseline; both processes exit 0. The WithLocalPeer SEND-side serialization (SerializeNewRouterWithLocalPeer + pab=true BeginProxyingToNewRouter) and the RequestMemory/ProvideMemory/AddBlockBuffer SEND round trip are sealed by the bypass court (routing.block-exhaustion-send). Not yet implemented: multi-subparcel/split parcels, node loss beyond the single link, and the acceptor-side bridge-bypass chain divergence (the oracle acceptor initiates its own bypass; the native replies only to the broker's — the same documented divergence as Phase 3). Reproduce: scripts/run_routing_court.sh

capabilities.name: Parcel-fragment allocation and free-list reuse (memory court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 memory court: the native memory-acceptor's parcel-fragment allocation, 256-byte pool exhaustion (inline fallback), and LIFO free-list reuse are byte-observable on the acceptor->broker wire and match the baseline byte-for-byte (modulo node names and per-link sequence numbers); the broker's event streams are byte-identical. The pinned mojo embedder sets IPCZ_MEMORY_FIXED_PARCEL_CAPACITY (crbug.com/40876289), disabling parcel-data expansion, so parcel-data-driven expansion stays disabled; the RouterLinkState-pool exhaustion trigger is sealed separately by the bypass court (routing.block-exhaustion-send), which exercises the RequestMemory/ProvideMemory/AddBlockBuffer SEND side. Reproduce: scripts/run_memory_court.sh

capabilities.name: Block-capacity exhaustion: AddBlockBuffer receive side (exhaustion court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 exhaustion court: 1486 held portal transfers exhaust the primary buffer's 64-byte RouterLinkState pool; the broker shares a new 64 KiB block buffer via AddBlockBuffer; the native exhaust-acceptor adopts it and resolves the remaining transfers' link states from it (cross-buffer fragment resolution), handles the exhausted-pool proxy transfer and the route migrations, and delivers the complete route sequence (rseq 0..1485); the broker's event streams are byte-identical. The RouterLinkState refcount lifecycle (allocation ref 1, link-creation ref, no-increment adoption, last-ref free; unmanaged fixed initial states) is implemented and sealed. Documented residual: the shared free-list reuse order differs by scheduler-dependent interleavings of the peer's IO-thread releases (the exhaustion point and the routing court's r1 reused block differ; block-reuse order is internal and normalized). Reproduce: scripts/run_exhaust_court.sh

capabilities.name: Block-capacity exhaustion SEND side: RequestMemory/ProvideMemory/AddBlockBuffer (bypass court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 bypass court: the ACCEPTOR's SerializeNewRouterWithLocalPeer transfers (new central link + decaying peripheral sublink per transfer, one RouterLinkState from the shared 64-byte pool each) exhaust the pool on the acceptor side; the unconditional TryAllocateRouterLinkState lobby sends RequestMemory to the broker (this node is the allocation delegate); the broker's ProvideMemory is adopted by on_provide_memory, which shares the new buffer via AddBlockBuffer (the native SEND, transmitted before the local registration) and registers it; the remaining transfers resolve their link states from the new buffer (cross-buffer fragment resolution). The broker's event stream is byte-identical to the oracle-acceptor baseline and all 1520 transfers plus the sync marker are verified; the send-side round trip is visible on the acceptor->broker wire in both runs. Forensic fix sealed by this court: the mojo-driver SharedBuffer object encoding (ObjectHeader{8, kSharedBuffer} + BufferHeader) is required by the official SharedBuffer::Deserialize; an empty driver object drops the broker's NodeLink. The failed run is preserved under evidence/bypass/20260805T185330Z/. Documented residual: the exhaustion point differs between runs (the oracle's concurrent IO thread frees payload fragments; the native's single-threaded loop does not wait) — internal block accounting, normalized; the broker's event stream is unaffected. Reproduce: scripts/run_bypass_court.sh

capabilities.name: Multi-node referral: broker + referrer A + referred B in both mixed-language pairings (3-node court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 3-node court, BOTH mixed-language pairings: interop-b = official broker + official referrer A + native referred B (3node-acceptor); interop-a = official broker + native referrer A (3node-referrer) + official referred B. The native B completes the referral handshake (ConnectToReferredBroker greeting without consuming a NodeLink sequence number; ConnectToReferredNonBroker acceptance), adopts the broker and referrer links with their initial portals, and triggers the OUTBOUND BypassPeer -> BypassPeerWithNewRemoteLink -> AcceptBypassLink(id 31) to the broker (bypass RouterLinkState {0,1088,64} + sublink 12 from the broker link memory; unreachable in 2-node graphs). The native A (referrer) sends ReferNonBroker before the shared-memory client handshake, adopts the A<->B link on NonBrokerReferralAccepted (EstablishWaitingRouters, service portal 0, a2b attachment bridge), re-transfers Y' with proxy_peer_node_name = the broker (the bypass lock records the full NodeName so the broker's CanNodeRequestBypass accepts B's AcceptBypassLink), forwards the un-consumed hello through the proxy, and runs the acceptor-side bootstrap bridge bypass with the waiting-bit wakeup (FlushRouter) that lets the broker's second stage and the pipe_a closure complete. In both pairings the broker's AND the counterpart's event streams are byte-identical; all four captured wire directions are structurally identical modulo node-name GUIDs. Re-sealed 2026-08-06 after the multi-link refactor regression fixes: the referrer's connect_handshake now records the broker link's remote_name in the links map (the proxy-peer descriptor must name the broker), and the transfer predicate matches the PORTAL handle type on any sublink (the b2a route's bridge self-bypass migrates the arrival sublink). Reproduce: scripts/run_3node_court.sh

capabilities.name: Introduction machinery: RequestIntroduction/AcceptIntroduction + EstablishLink -> BypassPeerWithNewRemoteLink (4-node court, both mixed-language pairings)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 4-node court: broker + referrer A + referred B + introduced C, all broker links relayed. A transfers Y through a2b (WithLocalPeer over the direct link); B re-transfers Y' through b2c with proxy_peer_node_name = A; C's router calls BypassPeer(A) with NO link to A and sends RequestIntroduction (id 10); the broker sends AcceptIntroduction (id 11, packed V0: single-byte link_side/remote_node_type at offset 16, transport + memory driver objects, V1 remote_features OFFSET field) to C (side A) and A (side B); C adopts the C<->A link and completes the bypass with AcceptBypassLink (id 31) over it; the hello/world round trip crosses the new link. Both pairings: interop-c (native 4node-acceptor) and interop-a (native 4node-referrer). The native implements router_bypass_peer with the establish_link fallback, the pending_introductions queue, on_accept_introduction (transport+buffer adoption), on_accept_bypass_link with CanNodeRequestBypass, and the per-link memory/sub-link multi-link generalizations. In each pairing the broker's AND counterpart nodes' event streams are byte-identical to the all-official baseline and all processes exit 0. Documented nondeterminism (normalized): the all-official baseline races on the pipe_a bridge-bypass exchange initiator (shared RouterLinkState lock CAS), so the broker<->A wire comparison drops the exchange messages + ordinal/seq prefixes; the fixed-point done/closure traffic on the final sublink is still compared exactly. Reproduce: scripts/run_4node_court.sh
